pages.text: $(bold)Aberrant traits are "double-edged swords": strong positives with a mandatory price.$(reset)$(br2)$(bold)【Tier 2 · Aberrations】$(reset)$(li)Berserker Gene (berserk_gene): +2 attack, −1.5 armor$(li)Glass Bones (glass_bone): +0.8 attack speed, −2 max health$(br2)$(bold)【Tier 3 · Aberrations】$(reset)$(li)Predator Instinct (predator_instinct): +3 attack, +2% move speed, −4 max health$(li)Pyroblast Flesh (pyroblast_flesh): +3 attack, $(reset)fears fire$(reset) — fire damage against you is greatly amplified$(br2)Higher tiers increase both the benefit and the cost.$(reset)

$(bold)Once attached, a trait cannot be removed$(reset) — aberrations are no exception.$(br2)$(bold)Your two ways out:$(reset)$(li)Hand the organ to the "$(l:akaishi:trait_reforger)Trait Reforger$(/l)" to swap that trait in place: it re-rolls within the same tier pool, so the aberration may be removed or drawn again$(li)Abandon the organ and grow a new one on the organ line$(br2)$(bold)Note:$(reset) aberrant traits are a high-risk, high-reward mechanic, not a defect; building around them usually beats repeated reforging.
Suggested order: aberrations roll from the same pool as safe traits — compare catalogs in "Safe Mutations"; use the "Trait Reforger" to swap an aberration away (or into) an organ.
